answer.rationale: The binding constraints are timing and slack, not preference: 14 days is too short to qualify and ramp a new primary while the line runs at 94% with no buffer, so switch_primary_vendor (memory_c2) and add_second_source (memory_c3) both put delivery at risk this cycle even though c2 is the memory that most directly promises the 18% cut. defer_decision is unavailable because the contract does not auto-renew — deferring is a supply gap, not a delay. Straight renew_incumbent concedes the cost mandate outright. That leaves negotiate_terms, but the obvious lever is already dead: the incumbent has refused to reopen price this cycle, which directly undercuts memory_c4's mechanism (benchmarking moves them on price). The live lever is memory_c6 — term structure and volume commitment unlocking pricing without reopening this cycle's rate card. That is why c6 is the one memory worth the verification slot: I need the original record to see what volume and duration were actually committed, whether the quoted savings were realized or merely quoted, and whether scope stayed intact. Every inherited memory here is a success story with no recorded failures, which is itself a signal that the archive is selection-biased toward whatever was done rather than what worked; I am treating each as one observation, not a rule. Downstream value risk is explicit: a multi-year commitment bought to satisfy a one-year 18% mandate transfers optionality out of future cycles and would defuse the credible switching threat that makes memory_c2's low-cost vendor useful as leverage — the cheap fix now is the thing that makes next year's negotiation weak. So I structure this small and guarded: a short bridge or first tranche with negotiated step pricing, explicit off-ramps, and no long lock-in, and I spend no line risk this cycle. Qualification of the low-cost vendor as a genuine second source stays queued for the next review, when there is buffer to absorb a ramp. If c6's source record shows the volume pricing required a lock-in longer or deeper than the memory implies, or that the savings were never verified, I fall back to a minimal bridge renewal at current terms and carry the cost gap forward rather than buying it with optionality I cannot get back.
